title: Corners open more doors
description: A corner mark belongs to three possible winning lines. A side square belongs to only two. Open wide.

title: The centre is the busiest square
description: The centre sits on four winning lines, more than any other square. Take it when you can.

title: Forks are double trouble
description: A fork threatens two wins at once. Your opponent can only block one of them.

title: A draw is a respectable result
description: Against perfect play, tic-tac-toe is a draw. Nobody loses when both sides stay sharp.

title: Block first, decorate later
description: If Mudi has two in a row, the third square is not a suggestion. It is a warning.

title: Nine squares, 255,168 games
description: That is how many ways a full board can play out. Most games are much shorter than you think.

title: X always moves first
description: The opener is chosen at random, but X gets the first mark. Being X is a small head start.

title: Mudi thinks in silences
description: Every computer move arrives after a deliberate pause. The board is not lagging; it is plotting.

title: The anti-diagonal is a trap
description: Squares 2, 4 and 8 form the quieter diagonal. Forks love it.

title: Perfect play has no winners
description: Minimax searches every reply before choosing. That is why the best you can usually do is draw.

title: Symmetry is a shortcut
description: Many openings are reflections of each other. Rotate the board and you may recognise the pattern.

title: One square can change everything
description: A single well-placed mark can turn a quiet board into a forced win.
